subject: Incident: p95 latency spike + throughput drop — mobilization & customer plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Incident: p95 latency spike + throughput drop — mobilization & customer plan

Team —

Observed a coordinated p95 latency spike and ~30% throughput degradation for BrightCart traffic starting ~08:45 PT. Alerting shows elevated queuing on gen-api frontends and elevated token compute times for a small subset of nodes. Running impact: several BrightCart endpoints exceeding their SLOs; CS flagged larger request fanouts.

Immediate asks:
- Ben / SRE: can you confirm whether this is kernel scheduling / preemption related vs. a KV cache miss storm? Quick triage checklist would help (kv hit ratios, recent kernel changes, machine restarts).
- Marissa / Eng PM: are there any recent rollouts or routing changes that could explain a region-specific regression?
- Karthik / Product: we need to align on temporary routing/fallback policy we can push to reduce p95 for BrightCart while we triage. Is a model-variant fallback acceptable?
- Soojin / Ops: can you stand up a capacity bump or resume reserved instances for the affected pool if needed?

I attached a short slowlog extract and a p95 timeseries snapshot. I'm drafting a customer note for Alex Barnes at BrightCart and would like a reviewed version within the hour so we can avoid them discovering the issue themselves.

Short term plan I propose: (1) emergency routing to a compat model variant for BrightCart only, (2) temporary QPS cap on any multi-call fanouts, (3) deep triage with SRE to identify root cause. Please reply with availability and quick wins.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: brightcart_slowlog_0521.txt, p95-timeseries-20260521.png

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident: p95 latency spike + throughput drop — mobilization & customer plan

Naomi —

Quick update from triage: we've scoped the event to a multi-tenant runtime lane (lane-30) servicing BrightCart and a few other customers. Preliminary signals:
- KV cache miss rate jumped ~6x starting 08:44.
- One recent kernel change (lightweight scheduler tweak) rolled two nights ago to a subset of the fleet; rollback window is possible but will cause brief disruption.
- No host-level restarts logged in the last 24h for affected pool.

Immediate remediation we can try in order (estimated time to impact):
1) Serve BrightCart from a compatible quantized variant (model KQV-2) restricted to low-latency path — low risk, ~5–10m to route and validate.
2) Toggle aggressive KV warmup and disable eviction for the affected cache shards — medium risk, ~15–30m to validate.
3) Rollback the scheduler tweak on the affected subpool — high-impact, needs coordination with eng and will require an ops window (~30–45m to rollback and validate).

I recommend option (1) + (2) in parallel to get fast relief while we evaluate scheduler rollback. Soojin, can you prepare the routing override to point BrightCart to the compat variant? Marcus, can you watch the KV shard metrics and confirm whether warmups improve hit rate?

I'll open INF-8241 on Jira and drop logs/trace links. Attaching a short extract (brightcart_slowlog_0521.txt) — looks like several requests hitting long tail token expansion on the same model shard.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: brightcart_slowlog_0521.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident: p95 latency spike + throughput drop — mobilization & customer plan

Thanks Ben —

Product constraints / considerations:
- Compatible model variant fallback is acceptable for BrightCart as a short-term mitigation, provided we document expected differences (tokenization edge cases, slight output distribution shifts). Need explicit signoff from Naomi for customer messaging.
- Avoid changing any model weights or quantization live; only routing to an already-verified variant.
- For routing override, we must check if BrightCart pinned to a specific model version in their tenant config. If pinned, we'll need an override at the routing layer rather than changing their default.

Roadmap asks (post-incident):
- We should prioritize a 'hot-warm' KV warmup design to prevent mass miss storms on restarts/evictions. Moving this to Q3 roadmap and assign an engineering epic would reduce similar incidents.
- Add a per-tenant compatibility flag so we can apply model-variant fallbacks without tenant config changes.

I'll start a short decision log item and can draft a follow-up PR for the feature ask. Naomi — I can help craft the customer note with a concise explanation of the fallback and expected behavior.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Group PM, Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@brightcart.com>
Cc: BrightCart Support <support@brightcart.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: [Draft] Brief: transient performance issue impacting some BrightCart endpoints (for review)

Alex —

We're proactively reaching out to let you know we observed a transient performance issue affecting a subset of BrightCart endpoints between ~08:45–09:15 PT today. Symptoms: higher-than-normal p95 latency and a reduced throughput on some high-fanout requests. We understand this could affect checkout/multi-call flows.

What we did immediately:
- Routed your traffic to a verified, lower-latency model variant (no model weight changes).
- Applied temporary QPS smoothing on multi-call fanouts to reduce downstream amplification.
- Opened a dedicated investigation (INF-8241) — our SRE and product teams are actively triaging root cause.

What you can expect:
- Short-term: we expect p95 latency to return to baseline within 15–30 minutes of the routing change.
- Mid-term: we will share a post-incident summary with root cause, timeline, and corrective actions within 48 hours.

Please let me know if you observed any customer-facing errors or if you want us to open a dedicated support ticket. We value your trust and will follow up with a detailed RCA.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference

---
[Internal note: Marissa/Karthik/Ben, please review wording. I want to avoid technical jargon for BrightCart but be transparent on actions. Attachment: cust-comm-draft-0521.md]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident: p95 latency spike + throughput drop — mobilization & customer plan

Thanks everyone — quick post-mobilization update:
- Routing override to model KQV-2 completed at 09:05 PT; BrightCart p95 improved from 420ms -> 115ms within two validation cycles.
- KV warmup toggle increased hit rate from 82% -> 93% by 09:30 PT; continued monitoring in place.
- Decision: do not rollback scheduler tweak yet; evidence points to cache evaporation cascade as primary vector.

Action items:
- Ben to produce preliminary traces & root-cause hypothesis for the RCA (INF-8241) by EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik to own the Q3 epic: hot-warm KV warmup design (create epic and assign engineers).
- Naomi to send the reviewed customer note to Alex and log the support ticket if they request dedicated handling.
- Soojin/Marcus to keep metrics dashboard open and escalate if hit rate dips below 88%.

Nice coordination — recommend we schedule a 30m postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 PT to capture triage timeline and finalize the communication.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
